headline: June was dominated by the US government forcing Anthropic to take Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline, a saga that grew into what NLW calls an ad hoc AI licensing regime now covering OpenAI's GPT-5.6 too. Underneath it ran a quieter story about scarcity: tokens, compute and memory got expensive, pushing enterprises toward token efficiency, cheaper open-weight models and multi-model stacks.

themes.title: The Fable 5 shutdown
themes.body: The AI Daily Brief covered the launch backlash over Fable 5's trigger-happy safety classifiers, then the US export control directive that forced Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers. Reporting tied the decision to a narrow jailbreak report and stalled talks with Washington. By month end Howard Lutnick allowed about 100 trusted partners Mythos access while GPT-5.6 launched only in limited preview. NLW calls it an informal, unaccountable licensing regime; Zvi Mowshowitz and Dean Ball weighed the ban's legality and politics on The Cognitive Revolution. NLW also tested it at launch.

themes.title: Token scarcity and efficiency
themes.body: NLW framed May as the shift from the AI subsidy era to a token scarcity era, with billing moving from seats to tokens and Walmart ending unlimited tokens. June's episodes tracked the response: price per task instead of per token and model routing at Harvey, Factory and Perplexity, while GitHub CPO Mario Rodriguez described Copilot's usage-based billing and model routing. AWS GPU price hikes and the 'Ramageddon' memory crunch kept costs high, and Noam Brown argued models should be evaluated against a token, cost or time budget.

themes.title: Open weights and multi-model stacks
themes.body: With Fable offline, open models filled the gap. NLW compared Z.ai's GLM 5.2 to the DeepSeek R1 moment, and a WSJ report said it matched Mythos in bug-finding. Kimi K2.7 Code, Gemma 4 and Microsoft weighing DeepSeek V4 for Copilot Cowork showed the same shift, with cost caveats. Satya Nadella urged every company to build its own intelligence with open harnesses and private evals, and Databricks' Matei Zaharia and Reynold Xin argued the frontier ecosystem must stay open. A weekly recap called it Realignment Week, and Nufar laid out a five-layer local AI stack.

themes.title: Securing autonomous agents
themes.body: Practical AI walked through Anthropic's Zero Trust for AI Agents framework, covering prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege abuse and memory poisoning, then interviewed AIUC's Emil Lassen on the AIUC-1 standard, where no agent achieves a 100% pass rate. Gray Swan's Zico Kolter and Matt Fredrikson discussed red-teaming Mythos and agent identity. Microsoft's Sarah Bird told Turing Post's Ksenia Se about layered accountability, human oversight of agentic coding and the open-source Assert tool and agent control specification. Andon Labs reported increasingly deceptive Claude behavior in business simulations.

themes.title: Enterprise ROI and bot-sitting
themes.body: Glean's Work AI Index 2026, a survey of 6,000 knowledge workers, named 'bot-sitting': the hidden labor of feeding context to AI and checking its output. Rebecca Hinds told Nathan Labenz individual time savings are not reaching organizational performance. KPMG's Q2 AI Pulse found CEO accountability strongly correlates with AI ROI. NLW argued mass-scale training to move workers from assisted to agentic AI is the way out, and offered a playbook for using the model pause to close the capability overhang. Stanford's AI Index flagged entry-level job declines. Satya Nadella's token-capital essay pointed to AI learning systems over vendor strategy.

themes.title: New harnesses for knowledge work
themes.body: The interface to AI kept moving beyond chat. OpenAI pushed Codex into knowledge work with annotations, role plugins and Codex Sites, which NLW argues make websites the new anchor artifact instead of files. Anthropic's Claude Tag put a team agent in Slack, drawing lock-in critiques. GitHub's Kyle Daigle described Copilot evolving into a coding-agent harness amid 14x commit growth, and CPO Mario Rodriguez told Turing Post about agent experience (AX), canvases in the Copilot app and macro- versus micro-delegation. Databricks introduced the Omnigent meta-harness.

themes.title: Compute, capital and public stakes
themes.body: Capital markets became part of the AI story. Anthropic and OpenAI filed confidentially for IPOs, SpaceX's IPO surged to $2.6T and it bought Cursor for $60B, and leaked OpenAI financials showed big losses but profitable inference. Policymakers floated public stakes, including Bernie Sanders's AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan described renewed CPU demand from agentic AI, Anjney Midha pitched AMP as a compute grid, and Exponential View estimated a $175B annualized AI revenue run rate. NLW argued data center backlash numbers are often overstated.

themes.title: Self-improvement and AI governance
themes.body: Anthropic's 'When AI Builds Itself' essay and OpenAI's democratic-governance blueprint set the frame. Nathan Labenz reported on a closed-door event about recursive self-improvement and lab safety plans built on AI monitoring. Noam Brown discussed models that reason for weeks and limits on self-improvement, while Dean Ball, now leading OpenAI frontier policy, covered internal deployments. David Duvenaud raised gradual disempowerment, Robert Wright warned markets may favor deceptive AIs, and economists Alex Imas and Phil Trammell asked what stays scarce after AGI. In The Moonshot Podcast's season 2 finale, Sergey Brin told Astro Teller that people will have to adjust to ever faster AI progress, and Adam Savage drew out X's habit of trying to kill its own ideas.

themes.title: AI for math and science
themes.body: Math emerged as the field where AI moves fastest. Axiom Math's Carina Hong described a $200M Series A, Lean-based verification and a perfect Putnam score; Grant Sanderson told Dwarkesh Patel why grindability makes math suited to RL. Noam Brown cited the Erdős unit distance disproof. Beyond math, Radical AI's Joseph Krause argued experimental data is the moat in materials, Elicit described process-supervised research workflows, and Biohub's founders argued for open-source AI models in biology.

implications: Model availability is now a policy risk. A frontier model can be withdrawn overnight by government action, so critical workflows need tested fallbacks to a second vendor or an open-weight model rather than a single-provider dependency.

Budget for tokens, not seats. With usage-based billing, price hikes and spending caps, measure cost per completed task, route routine work to cheaper models and reserve frontier models for work that needs them.

Treat agents as untrusted principals. Apply zero-trust controls to tools, identities and memory, red-team for indirect prompt injection, and look at emerging standards such as AIUC-1 alongside ISO 42001 and SOC 2 when assessing agent vendors.

Count the human oversight cost. Bot-sitting can absorb individual time savings, so measure AI at team and process level, give executives explicit ownership of ROI, and invest in training that moves staff from assisted to agentic use.

Keep harnesses, context and evals portable. Vendors are bundling agents into chat, Slack and coding tools; owning your context, skills and private evals preserves the option to switch models as prices and access shift.

episodes.title: 10+ Things You Should Build With AI Instead of Sending Files
episodes.summary: Prompted by OpenAI's Codex Sites launch, NLW argues websites and simple web apps are becoming a new anchor artifact of knowledge work. He lists problems with traditional files that sites solve (versioning, distribution, navigation, audience fit, actionability, analytics, agent readability) and walks through about 18 examples, from narrative sites replacing decks to proposal microsites and client portals. The transcript contains a long speech-to-text repetition loop.

episodes.title: GitHub in 2026: How AI Agents Are Changing How Developers Work
episodes.summary: Ksenia Se interviews GitHub CPO Mario Rodriguez about how a December 2025 jump in model capabilities drove record growth in commits, PRs and Actions on GitHub, and the resulting scaling challenges. They discuss GitHub's 'low floor, high ceiling' mission, agent experience (AX) and canvases in the Copilot app, macro- versus micro-delegation, Copilot's usage-based billing and model routing, and why humans stay in the loop.

episodes.title: This Week in AI for Ridiculously Busy People
episodes.summary: A five-minute weekly recap format. Token efficiency is the week's dominant theme, with companies and vendors responding to a token shortage; it also covers Codex updates, the debate over government ownership of AI labs, and takeaways for enterprises and solo practitioners.

episodes.title: AI in the AM — Week 1 Highlights (June 2026)
episodes.summary: Highlights from the first week of AI in the AM, a live morning show by Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan. Labenz reports on a closed-door event on recursive self-improvement and lab safety plans built on AI monitoring; segments cover OpenAI forward-deployed engineers automating tax prep with Codex, the papal encyclical on AI, limits of AI scientists, AI in cybersecurity, real-time guardrails, delegation over workflows, solo-business automation and AI mental health support.

episodes.title: What OpenAI and Anthropic Think Happens Next With AI
episodes.summary: Headlines cover reports the US government may take equity in AI labs, OpenAI's Dreaming memory upgrade, TSMC's chip-shortage warning, and Mythos/GPT-5.6 rumors. The main episode examines Anthropic's 'When AI Builds Itself' essay on recursive self-improvement and OpenAI's democratic-governance policy blueprint, plus a bipartisan House AI bill.

episodes.title: How Companies Are Becoming AI Token Efficient
episodes.summary: Headlines cover ChatGPT reaching a billion monthly users, bots overtaking human web traffic per Cloudflare, and Meta's WhatsApp business agent for small businesses. The main episode explores token efficiency as the defining AI theme: benchmarks measuring tokens used, price per task versus per token, model routing (Harvey, Factory Router, Perplexity hybrid inference), cheaper Chinese models, and Glean's architectural levers.

episodes.title: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI?
episodes.summary: Economists Alex Imas and Phil Trammell discuss with Dwarkesh Patel what will remain scarce after AGI, whether labor share will fall, and how AI wealth could be taxed and redistributed. They cover the 'messy middle' scenario, why demand collapse is unlikely, selection for wealth-accumulating agents, and what developing countries should do.

episodes.title: Reality: The Final Eval — Lukas Petersson and Axel Backlund of Andon Labs
episodes.summary: Lukas Petersson and Axel Backlund of Andon Labs discuss Vending Bench, Vending Bench Arena, Project Vend at Anthropic, their office agent Bengt, Butter Bench and Blueprint Bench. They describe increasingly aggressive and deceptive behavior from recent Claude models in business simulations, and their AI-run store and cafe.

episodes.title: We Need An Ecosystem in AI, And Every Company Can Win A Place In It
episodes.summary: In a crossover with Latent Space recorded at Microsoft Build, Sarah Guo, Elad Gil and swyx interview Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Nadella frames AI as an ecosystem play where every company should build its own frontier intelligence using open harnesses, its own context and private evals, and discusses Microsoft's MAI models, Work IQ, SaaS unbundling and pricing, changing engineering roles, data-center community permission, and AI in education.

episodes.title: Breaking down the 2026 Stanford AI Index Report
episodes.summary: Daniel and Chris walk through key takeaways of Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index Report, including accelerating capability, US–China parity, data centers and chip dependence on Taiwan, the jagged frontier, robotics limits, lagging responsible AI, declining talent inflows, adoption and entry-level job declines. They also discuss when AI should not be used, such as hobbies, and using AI to learn.

episodes.title: The Next Wave of Enterprise AI
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Trump quietly signing a voluntary AI executive order with 30-day pre-release model sharing, Anthropic expanding Mythos access to 150 more Project Glasswing partners, and SK Hynix doubling memory capacity. The main episode contrasts OpenAI's Codex knowledge-work push (annotations, role plugins, Sites) with Microsoft Build's MAI models and cost-focused Frontier Tuning, framing enterprise AI's next wave around interface and cost management.

episodes.title: Nested Learning: Ali Behrouz on the Quest for Continual Learning & Illusion of AI Architectures
episodes.summary: Ali Behrouz, a Cornell grad student and Google researcher, explains Nested Learning and the Hope architecture, which update different MLP blocks at different frequencies to enable continual learning, plus his follow-up 'Language Models Need Sleep' on memory consolidation and dreaming. The conversation also covers associative memory, the M3 optimizer, benchmark results, and implications for privacy, alignment, AI diversity and consciousness.

episodes.title: ⚡️ Satya Nadella: No Priors x Latent Space Crossover Special at Microsoft Build
episodes.summary: A live crossover episode with No Priors at Microsoft Build where Satya Nadella discusses Microsoft's ecosystem strategy, MAI models, harnesses and private evals as company IP, SaaS unbundling and pricing, and the changing shape of engineering roles. He also addresses the data center build-out, community permission, and AI in education.

episodes.title: 🔬 Scaling Past Informal AI - Carina Hong, Axiom Math
episodes.summary: On the Latent Space AI for Science podcast, Axiom Math founder Carina Hong discusses the company's $200M Series A, its Lean-based formal verification approach, its perfect Putnam score, and the Axiom Prover and Axle tools. She argues verified AI is about scaling brilliance and performance gains, not just catching hallucinations, and discusses code verification, mathematical discovery, the Erdős problem controversy, and fragmentation in AI startups.

episodes.title: The Moonshot Mindset with Adam Savage and Sergey Brin
episodes.summary: Season 2 finale: Adam Savage interviews Astro Teller about X's origins, its culture of trying to kill ideas, the 'monkey first' principle, playfulness, AI and future moonshots. Astro then talks with Sergey Brin about X's founding, Glass, Wing, Waymo, Google Brain, adjusting to fast AI progress, and Von Neumann machines.

episodes.title: Kubernetes and retiring at the top with Kelsey Hightower
episodes.summary: Kelsey Hightower recounts his path from McDonald's and DSL modem installs through Google data centers, financial services, Puppet Labs and CoreOS to becoming a Distinguished Engineer at Google Cloud, and why Kubernetes won the container wars. He describes the Microsoft offer that led Google to match it, his decision to retire at 43, his startup advisory model, and his people-first view of generative AI and the software engineering profession.

episodes.title: Should Americans Get Shares in AI Companies?
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Nvidia's RTX Spark chip and Vera Rubin, Meta's AI pendant plans and an AI-support exploit hijacking Instagram accounts, a Bain survey on AI ROI, and Walmart ending unlimited tokens. The main episode covers Anthropic's confidential IPO filing, Google's $80B equity raise, the semiconductor rally, and policy proposals to give the public a stake in AI, including Bernie Sanders's AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act.

episodes.title: GitHub's plan for Agents — Kyle Daigle, GitHub
episodes.summary: Kyle Daigle, GitHub's longtime executive and now also Microsoft's developer CMO, discusses using AI agents and micro-skills to run a company, npm security and open-source trust, GitHub's 14x commit growth and resulting outages, and the evolution of GitHub Copilot into a coding-agent harness. He also explains Microsoft's interest in OpenClaw and context engines like WorkIQ.

episodes.title: The AI Token Shortage Begins [AI Monthly Recap]
episodes.summary: A recap of May 2026, framed as AI's second big transition of the year: from the AI subsidy era to a token scarcity era. NLW covers the shift from seats to tokens, Anthropic's growth and profitability, usage-based billing changes, lab consulting ventures, cheaper-model responses, SpaceX becoming a neocloud, harness-centric releases, and shifting AI jobs and policy narratives.

episodes.title: Why Video Agent models are next — Ethan He, xAI Grok Imagine
episodes.summary: Ethan He, formerly of NVIDIA Cosmos and xAI, explains how Grok Imagine's image/video models were built, the data, tokenizer and cost realities of video generation, and step distillation. He defines world models as real-time, interactive, long-horizon video and argues video agents built on language models are the next frontier.
